chunks: 65 - Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar from Muhammad ibn Isa from Abu Ali ibn Rashid who said:

I said to him (peace be upon him), 'May I be your ransom, indeed the removal of shade is difficult for me while in the state of Ihram because I am Mahroom (sensitive to sun/heat), and the sun is intense on me.' He said, 'Shade yourself and pay one Damm.' I said to him, 'One Damm or two Dams?' He said, 'For Umrah.' I said, 'We enter Ihram with Umrah, enter Mecca, then become Halal, and then enter Ihram with Hajj.' He said, 'Then pay two Dams.' And if the Muhrim is with a companion who is ill/sick, he should shade him and not shade himself. This was narrated.

66 - Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Bakr ibn Salih who said: I wrote to Abu Ja'far al-Thani (peace be upon him), 'My aunt is with me and she is my Zamilah (companion in travel/Ihram), and the heat is intense on her when she enters Ihram. Do you think I should shade her and myself?' He wrote back, 'Shade her alone.'

key_terms.إِحْرَام: Ihram (state of consecration for Hajj or Umrah)
key_terms.ظَلِّل: Shade yourself (wear a hat or use an umbrella)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling and compensation for a pilgrim who cannot tolerate the sun while in Ihram?
ai.summary: These narrations from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* detail the fiqh of *Tathallu* (shading) for the Muhrim, distinguishing between the single *Damm* (one sheep) for Umrah and the double *Damm* for Hajj, reflecting the severity of the restriction. The second narration highlights the scholarly principle of prioritizing the relief of the sick or weak companion over the self, illustrating the practical application of *Rukhsah* (concession) in ritual purity and sacrifice.
